name: Kingdom of Thailand
native: ราชอาณาจักรไทย (Ratcha-anachak Thai)
ประเทศไทย (Prathet Thai)

predecessors.name: Rattanakosin Kingdom (Siam)
predecessors.text: the whole of the absolute monarchy of Siam, which became a constitutional monarchy on 24 June 1932

ledger.x: 1932: Siam becomes a constitutional monarchy (24 June).
1941: France cedes Laotian and Cambodian territory to Thailand.
1942: the Thai Phayap Army takes the Shan States.
1943: Japan hands four northern Malay states to Thailand.
1945: the northern Malay states leave Thai hands.
1946: Thailand returns the Laotian and Cambodian territory taken in 1941.

wars.name: Franco-Thai War
wars.outcome: Thai victory on the ground; a Japanese-mediated armistice (31 January 1941) and the Tokyo peace treaty (9 May) gave Thailand Laotian and Cambodian provinces; Thailand had to pay six million piastres and accepted only a quarter of the territory it had won.

wars.name: Thai Phayap Army campaign in the Shan States
wars.outcome: Thailand, allied to Japan, occupied Kengtung and the Shan States from May 1942, fought the retreating Chinese 93rd Division, and held the Shan States until August 1945.

certainty.note: Judgment: a modern surveyed frontier throughout; no page opened gives demarcation dates.
